_comment: Function-level vulnerable-export data for well-documented npm CVEs. Package-level CVE feeds (OSV/GHSA/NVD) tell you a bad *version* is in your tree; almost none tell you which *exported function* actually carries the vulnerable code path, which is the piece reachability analysis needs. This file is hand-curated from each advisory's technical writeup so the demo traversal is grounded in real, checkable vulnerabilities rather than invented ones. A production build would maintain this as a continuously-updated feed, not a static file.

entries.summary: lodash.template allows command injection through the `options.imports` template variable when template source or options are attacker-influenced; the compiled template function evaluates using the Function constructor.
minimist's argument parser mutates Object.prototype when a crafted `--__proto__` flag is parsed, giving prototype pollution to any caller that passes untrusted argv straight into minimist.

node-serialize.unserialize executes embedded IIFE payloads in the serialized string via eval-equivalent deserialization, giving remote code execution on any input the attacker can influence, e.g. a cookie.

ejs.render does not sufficiently sanitize the `settings` / `options` object; an attacker who controls render options (common when options are built from request-derived data) can achieve template-string-based remote code execution.

jsonwebtoken.verify can be tricked into using an attacker-supplied value as the signing secret when the secret/key lookup is dynamic and untrusted input reaches the algorithm or key-selection path, allowing signature forgery.
lodash.merge is vulnerable to prototype pollution when merging an attacker-controlled object, letting an attacker inject or overwrite properties on Object.prototype.
